comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Final line of the proof of Theorem 2.6: "properly proximal relative to $\Gamma(\cap_{v\in\mathcal V(\mathcal G)}\mathrm{link}(v))=\mathbb C$".

To conclude full proper proximality from Lemma 2.4, one needs $\bigcap_{v}\mathrm{link}(v)=\varnothing$, i.e. no vertex $w$ lies in $\mathrm{link}(v)$ for **every** $v$.

**Required (graph-theoretic):** prove from irreducibility and $|\mathcal V(\mathcal G)|\ge3$ that no vertex is adjacent to all others. A vertex $w$ adjacent to all others would give the join decomposition $\mathcal V=\{w\}\sqcup(\mathcal V\setminus\{w\})$ with every pair across the partition an edge — contradicting irreducibility (here $|\mathcal V|\ge3$ ensures $\mathcal V\setminus\{w\}$ is nonempty and the partition is nontrivial). Conclude $\bigcap_v\mathrm{link}(v)=\varnothing$. (Note $w\notin\mathrm{link}(w)$, so the diagonal is already excluded; confirm the intersection is genuinely empty.)

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolution of prob-10-9.**

I addressed the final-line gap in the proof of the main theorem (Theorem 2.6), namely justifying $\bigcap_{v\in\mathcal V(\mathcal G)}\mathrm{link}(v)=\varnothing$ so that $\Gamma(\cap_v\mathrm{link}(v))=\mathbb C$ and full proper proximality follows from Lemma (Stability of relative proper proximality under intersections).

**Key observation.** With the link defined as $\mathrm{link}(v)=\{u:u\neq v,\,(u,v)\in\mathcal E\}$, we have $v\notin\mathrm{link}(v)$ for every $v$. The intersection $\bigcap_{v\in\mathcal V}\mathrm{link}(v)$ ranges over *all* vertices, so for any candidate $w\in\mathcal V$ the index $v=w$ is admissible; membership of $w$ in the intersection would force $w\in\mathrm{link}(w)$, a contradiction. Hence the intersection is empty. This is a complete, rigorous proof and, importantly, it holds for **any** finite graph, requiring neither $|\mathcal V|\ge3$ nor irreducibility.

I verified numerically (20000 random irreducible graphs with $|\mathcal V|\in\{3,\dots,6\}$, and 20000 arbitrary graphs with $|\mathcal V|\in\{1,\dots,6\}$) that $\bigcap_v\mathrm{link}(v)$ is empty in every case, consistent with the diagonal argument.

**On the critic's suggested route.** The critic proposed deriving emptiness from irreducibility via the join decomposition $\mathcal V=\{w\}\sqcup(\mathcal V\setminus\{w\})$. That argument is valid but proves a *stronger* (and here unnecessary) statement: that no vertex is adjacent to all others. Emptiness of the intersection of links itself follows immediately from the diagonal exclusion $w\notin\mathrm{link}(w)$ and does not need irreducibility. I made the diagonal argument fully explicit in the text and added a parenthetical remark recording the join-decomposition fact (with the $|\mathcal V|\ge3$ note ensuring the complementary part $\mathcal V\setminus\{w\}$ is nonempty), while clarifying that the diagonal observation already suffices.

**Edit made to `solution.tex`** (Conclusion paragraph of "Proof of the main theorem"): expanded the one-line justification into an explicit contradiction argument, noted nonemptiness of the indexing family, added the irreducibility remark, and stated $\Gamma(\varnothing)=\mathbb C\,1$ explicitly, concluding proper proximality relative to $\mathbb C$.
